### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**24** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b8ca361c0662bfc2bfff31de86bd6b4ad0802e4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e0b1bf39d40d422eea67b9661a3121e2fda090b0` — the merge of head `d830f5af03cc2ddb4e481c0b78522447e9825c58` into base `5b8ca361c0662bfc2bfff31de86bd6b4ad0802e4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e0b1bf39d40d422eea67b9661a3121e2fda090b0 && git checkout e0b1bf39d40d422eea67b9661a3121e2fda090b0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5b8ca361c0662bfc2bfff31de86bd6b4ad0802e4 d830f5af03cc2ddb4e481c0b78522447e9825c58 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5b8ca361c0662bfc2bfff31de86bd6b4ad0802e4 && git merge --no-ff d830f5af03cc2ddb4e481c0b78522447e9825c58

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5b8ca361c0662bfc2bfff31de86bd6b4ad0802e4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

**What changed since the body was written.**

- `fe0f53eb`: the engine-double ledger (`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`) records the new rest pin's `findOne` double; this was the engine-double-contract red at 48c654cc.
- `7ddcc646`: at fe0f53eb, `Test Core (3/10)` was red on `packages/runtime/src/mcp-list-objects-statements.pin.test.ts` ("the delegated callers pay their delegator once"): the memo `list_objects` read paid 31 statements at 150 objects against a bound of 24. "A title equal to the owner's reads the pair's translation first, then the deployment's" is true only when another tab title of the same object diverges. When none diverges, every title reads the deployment catalog, which already deep-merges the pair's share, as before this PR. The controls pin both cases.

  - rest `tsc --noEmit` exit 0;

- Dogfood battery (the `(narrowing)` arm and the `!` title), `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under `os-verify-lock` at fe0f53eb: `VERDICT command-exit 0`, `Test Files 490 passed | 3 skipped (493)`, `Tests 4144 passed | 68 skipped (4212)`. 7ddcc646 only reduces when the object read asks the pair.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7ddcc64690282bb66f2c8baf5d8ea0aacf080884`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.translation-related-list-key-under-arrangement-refused.ts (the published-schema hit), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-object-related-list-pair-i18n.test.ts, packages/lint/src/related-list-titles.ts, packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, packages/lint/src/i18n-related-lists-arrangement-36595.test.ts, packages/cli/test/i18n-coverage.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-related-lists-label-translation-36528.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts (`labelCatalogs`, `translateObjectRelatedLists`, `valueOverridesPackagedBase`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts (`getPairTranslationBundle`), packages/core/src/fallbacks/authored-translation-sync.ts (`readAuthoredTranslationLayer`), packages/lint/src/object-graph.ts (`objectExtensionsByTarget`), packages/runtime/src/mcp-list-objects-statements.pin.test.ts, AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3)

Inputs: card #37622 (body and its five comments, the claim and the os-dev-report included), PR #38085 (body, the final-head comment 7232875384, the net diff against merge base `815e882b`), and the check-runs on the head: 70 runs, 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`os validate` accept set: unchanged. Right.** The fold in `related-list-titles.ts` is the block removed from `validate-translation-references.ts`, with the same order (owner, every placement, then each arrangement in two passes) and the same membership. A placement labels a list only where none is labelled yet, which gives the same label set as before. Only the two hints and the stripped message change their words.
- **`collectExpectedEntries` expected key set: changed, and declared. Right.** Under a `.custom` arrangement it no longer expects a key over a list the arrangement hides, names bare or re-states with no label, and it newly expects a key over a list the arrangement labels. That second half can turn a passing `os i18n check --strict` red, which is the narrowing the changeset declares. A placement-only label is still not expected, as on `main`.
- **Served `/meta/object` answer: changed, on both reads. Right.** A tab title that departs from the packaged base now reads the pair's own translation, where it kept its own text. No export, option or route is added: `TranslateDocumentOptions` and `i18n-resolver.ts` are not in the diff, and `objectPairRelatedListsBundleOf` and `hasRelatedListTitleOffBase` are module-private.
- **Ledger entry `translation-related-list-key-under-arrangement-refused` (published in `@objectstack/spec`): wording only. Right.** `surface`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` now match the code: a label equal to the owner's reads the deployment catalog, any other label reads the pair's translation.
- **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: one new row, right.** It records the single `findOne` double of the new rest test. It is the engine-double ledger, not the statement budget.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the changeset and the PR body carry the same line, and it is the right arm: the coverage gate can newly refuse a stack that passed.

`Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No key, accepted value or metadata type moves; what moves is a tooling expectation and a served translation. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3, `none` takes `patch`, and a breaking non-protocol change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition. The changeset has all three for `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/spec`, and the remedy (add the translation, or drop the entry's `label`) is in the body. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the os-dev-report.
- **Author point (1), the statement budget: the gate keeps the promised behaviour and the budget is honest.** See ④ for the reading.
- **Author point (2), the body sentence: a body wording fix, not a contract defect.** See ④.
- **Skills follow-up** (`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md`, `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`): the text there is still correct, only no longer the single remedy. `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` stands; the seat files the card.
- **Placement-only label accepted by the rule and not scaffolded:** unchanged from `main`, and the accepting direction. It leaves one coverage gap that predates this PR: where the owner declares `relatedLists` and does not name the placed list, the registry does apply the placement, the title is served, and `os i18n check` does not count it. For the seat to file; not a finding on this head.
- **Public form route with no pair bundle:** accepted. A public form draws no record-page tabs.
- **A pair translation outranks any diverged tab title, whoever wrote it:** answered by ruling record 6631250894 (a pair translation, then the override's own text), and `withoutStaleObjectPlural` (#30391) already applies that order to an object on any divergence.
- **Deviation, PR body not patched after the last two commits:** see N1.
- **SQL push-down:** no new in-app join or id materialisation. The one new read is `getPairTranslationBundle`, one filtered `sys_metadata` read bound to the pair's package. The list read memoises it per base for the page, and since `7ddcc646` it is asked only for an object with a diverged tab title.
- Out of the diff, for the seat: the read serves a diverged title from the pair's own `translation` rows only. Lint cannot tell which package ships a translation, so a stack that holds the owner and the arrangement can satisfy `os validate` and `os i18n check` with a translation shipped outside the pair, which the read does not use. This follows from #36574 and route R1, not from this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself.** It does not take a declared capability away at the consumer. Item 1 makes the refusal PR #37600 published real in the two commands that still contradicted it, so one key is no longer demanded by one gate and refused by another. Item 2 delivers a capability the rule has declared since #36574 (a key over a list the arrangement labels is accepted) by implementing it at the read, which is route R1 and the right direction: implemented, not narrowed.

**Scope of the pair bundle at the read.** Only `objects.NAME._relatedLists` per locale is handed on. Read against `labelCatalogs`: a changed string of the object reads the slice, which answers nothing outside tab titles, so it keeps its text as it did with no pair bundle; an unchanged string reads the slice laid over the deployment catalog, which is the deployment catalog for every other key. ADR-0146 D10 holds, and the scope pin covers it (the renamed `label` stays `Client`).

**Author point (1): the gate.** `hasRelatedListTitleOffBase` asks the question `translateObjectRelatedLists` asks, entry by entry: an object-form entry with a non-empty `list` and a non-empty `label`, compared with the first packaged entry of the same `list`, a missing one counting as diverged. That is `valueOverridesPackagedBase` over the same two documents the translator is then given. So the gate is true exactly when at least one title would read the pair-only catalog, and every title the arrangement sets or changes still reads the pair's translation. The changeset's promise is kept in full.

The budget is honest. `packages/runtime/src/mcp-list-objects-statements.pin.test.ts` is not in the diff, so the bound of 24 was met and not raised, and `Test Core (3/10)` is success on this head. The json row is the engine-double ledger's count for the new test file, which is what that gate asks for. The sixth rest pin counts zero pair asks for an object with no arrangement and for one that keeps the owner's title, and more than zero for one that relabels.

**Author point (2): the body sentence.** With the gate, a title equal to the owner's reads the pair first only when another title of the same object diverges; otherwise it reads the deployment catalog, exactly as on `main`. The deployment catalog already holds the pair's rows above every code bundle (`readAuthoredTranslationLayer` builds both from the same rows), so the served text is the same in both cases. It can differ in one corner only: two authored `translation` rows of different packages translating the same `_relatedLists` key, where the merged catalog keeps the later row by name. That corner behaves as it does on `main` unless a sibling title diverges. Neither the changeset nor the ledger entry promises pair-first for an equal title; the ledger says such a label "reads the deployment's translation". So the contract is whole and the sentence is wrong only in the PR body.

**Tried and held.** A relabel to the owner's own text (not diverged, deployment catalog); a title on a list the owner names bare (diverged, pair); a locale the pair does not ship (own text kept); a pair that translates nothing for the object (no bundle handed, so the translator answers as before); a hidden entry beside a bare child, both orders (pinned).

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — PR body. The sentence "A title equal to the owner's reads the pair's translation first, then the deployment's" should say this holds only when another tab title of the object diverges, and otherwise the title reads the deployment catalog. The body also still says the gate sweep is "running at 48c654cc", the dogfood battery is "owed", and the two-minute check shows 5 passing (it is 6). The final-head comment has the right readings; move them into the body, which is what the approver reads. A body edit does not move the head.
- N2 (nit) — `meta-object-related-list-pair-i18n.test.ts`, control "…and the pair first where it ships one". After `7ddcc646` that case asks the pair zero times; `人员` comes from the harness's deployment catalog, which lays the pair over the base. The assertion is right and the title misdescribes it. Left as an accepted deviation, or a follow-up: a fix moves the head.
- N3 (nit) — `translateMetaDocument` passes no memo, so the by-name read of an object that both renames its `label` with no plural and diverges a tab title asks `getPairTranslationBundle` twice (once here, once in `withoutStaleObjectPlural`). One extra read on a rare shape, no effect on the answer. Follow-up.

## Contract review brief — PR #38085 @ `7ddcc64690282bb66f2c8baf5d8ea0aacf080884` (card #37622)

Inputs — these and nothing else:

  · PR #38085: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `7ddcc64690282bb66f2c8baf5d8ea0aacf080884`
  · the check-runs on `7ddcc64690282bb66f2c8baf5d8ea0aacf080884`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the narrowing is declared of the whole PR, never of a path: the floor is EVERY path of the diff outside the
  prose faces (.changeset/37622-related-list-keys-agree-under-arrangement.md, content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx), plus every file those hunks make a claim about, read in the cited code.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below that floor; the record's `Scope:` line lists both. No path is the lane seat's remainder.
  ④ judges the narrowing itself over that floor: lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in
  the PR are not reviewed; the published spec and the cited code are READ to judge it, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-38085/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — the narrowing itself, read against the published spec on `main`: does it take a
     declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real? A capability declared
     and not delivered is an implementation gap, implemented or retired, ⛔ never narrowed at the consumer.
     Read the spec and the cited code in the live tree, and try to break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.
